# RESULTS_METHOD_v9.md — the citable number set

**GENERATED BY `src/v9_make_results.py` on 2026-08-29. Do not hand-edit.**
Every number is read from a v9 artifact at generation time; regenerate rather than correct.

**Citation rule (CLOSEOUT_V9 §4.2): this file is the single source. Numbers in `RESULTS_METHOD.md`, `RESULTS_V8.md`, `V8_FINDINGS.md` and all earlier result files are AS-RUN and are superseded.** They were measured with the collateral-gate float bug present.

---

## 0. What changed, and why every number moved

`collateral_ok` compared MMLU in floating point: `(pre - post) <= 0.02`. MMLU is scored on 200 items, so a 4-item drop **is** exactly the budget, but `0.545 - 0.525 == 0.020000000000000018 > 0.02`. Configurations sitting precisely on budget were rejected.

The v9 gate (`src/v9_gate.py`) compares in **integer items**: `(pre_items - post_items) <= 4`. No epsilon, nothing to tune. Verified exhaustively: across all 201x201 accuracy pairs on the 1/200 grid the old and new gates disagree on exactly **138** pairs, and **every one is a 4-item drop**.

Re-scoring every panel from persisted alpha traces recovered **714 probes/rows** and changed **146 cell values** across 32 panels.

### Panels that CANNOT be re-scored

| panel | rows | why |
|---|---:|---|
| `t2x` | 144 | no alpha_trace and no per-config collateral; predates the v6 trace fix. Boundary exposure UNKNOWN. |
| `v1` | 126 | no alpha_trace and no per-config collateral; predates the v6 trace fix. Boundary exposure UNKNOWN. |
| `v6trace/ste` | 24 | no alpha_trace and no per-config collateral; predates the v6 trace fix. Boundary exposure UNKNOWN. |
| `x` | 54 | no alpha_trace and no per-config collateral; predates the v6 trace fix. Boundary exposure UNKNOWN. |
| `x2` | 108 | no alpha_trace and no per-config collateral; predates the v6 trace fix. Boundary exposure UNKNOWN. |

These predate the v6 alpha-trace fix and store only a scalar removal, so there is no record of which alphas were probed. **Their boundary exposure is unknown and is not assumed to be zero.**

Contribution 4 stays **conditional**.

## 6. Reproducibility statement (re-scoped, WS2)

> Sweep-pipeline bit-determinism verified (108/108, results/x2 vs v6trace/x2, 0 differing). MMLU scoring is deterministic within a fixed environment and batch size (6/6 replicates identical) but exhibits batch-composition sensitivity of up to 1% (2 of 200 items); cross-version comparisons can differ by the same order. Fixed for v9 by scoring the gate in integer items, which removes the boundary knife-edge; NOT fixed at the source, which would require pinning batch composition and re-running.

Measured conditions (200 MMLU items, llama-3.2-3B-Instruct):

| condition | items | spread |
|---|---|---:|
| A_repeat_bs6 | [129, 129, 129] | 0 |
| B_batch_size | [131, 129, 131, 129] | 2 |
| C_tf32 | [129, 129] | 0 |
| D_n_rot | [129, 127] | 2 |
| E_cross_process_bs6 | [129, 129, 129] | 0 |

Attribution of the observed cross-panel divergence: The v8spc/small vs v6trace/ablate divergence (llama|occ_gender|s2) occurred at NOMINALLY IDENTICAL batch_size=6, so batch composition does not explain it. The remaining difference between those runs is the environment: the ablate panel was produced under transformers 5.14.1 and v8spc under 4.57.1 (the rebuild recorded in RESULTS_V8 2). This is consistent with the scoped determinism claim -- the edit CONSTRUCTION is bit-identical across that change, the MMLU EVALUATION is not. Not proven by re-running the old stack; stated as the residual explanation.

## 7. D1 — surgical MMLU re-run: NO

CLOSEOUT_V9 §WS2.3 says count first, then decide, and expected "dozens". The count is **833 probes within +-1 item of the 4-item budget — 10.5% of all 7960 probes** (463 at 3 items, 241 at 4, 129 at 5). A surgical re-run of those rows means re-training and re-evaluating their cells, i.e. re-running most panels. **Decision: default arm — keep trace values, let the integer gate absorb the boundary, and document the granularity as measurement noise.** The forward fix (>=1000 MMLU items so the budget is not 4x the metric's granularity) is a paper limitation and a repo issue, not a pre-deadline task.
